summary: Configured node1 as the cluster’s restricted internal NTP server and node2 to use node1 exclusively. Both nodes report normal synchronization, and configuration survived sequential node restarts.
actions_performed: Backed up /etc/chrony.conf on both nodes as /etc/chrony.conf.infraset.bak.
Configured node1 chronyd to permit NTP queries from node2 only.
Added a persistent node1 firewalld rule permitting UDP/123 from node2 only.
Removed public time sources from node2 and configured 10.100.90.10 (node1) as its sole preferred source.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially and verified changed boot identities and full recovery.

evidence.requirement: node1 operates as the internal time source
evidence.summary: Chronyd is active/enabled and synchronized at stratum 4; UDP/123 is listening, access and firewall rules restrict service to node2, and server-side statistics record node2 requests.
Only 10.100.90.10 is configured; node1 is selected with ^*, node2 is stratum 5, and Leap status is Normal.
Healthy baseline boot ID 3dba43a5-f3bc-4eb9-90a0-cacb0623feda, acknowledged reboot, changed boot ID acde444c-582b-47bf-b387-7eb39633596c, recovered synchronized server, and node2 reselected it.

Healthy baseline boot ID 0d6209e2-350d-4cd9-8a7d-11f7c08072be, acknowledged reboot, changed boot ID 3a199227-8f9a-4669-a663-2620894e46e6, and recovered active synchronization exclusively through node1.
